stops.note: the silk-cotton tree (Ceiba pentandra) is native to tropical America and West Africa but was widely planted on Java, which by the early 1900s supplied most of the world's kapok
light, buoyant and water-repellent, it stuffed mattresses and filled the life jackets issued in World War II

current_meaning: a fine fluffy fibre from the silk-cotton tree, used as stuffing
